optionalAcceptance.requirement: Equivalent BullMQ/Workflows benchmark records output parity, startup/runtime latency, recovery, concurrency and total cost; architecture review records adopt/defer for named capabilities with working rollout flags and rollback

sourceEvidence.title: Current repository authority
sourceEvidence.observation: The November 3 override makes Codex Lead/Technical Lead the coordinator, preserves independent review and exact-head founder merge authority, and removes mandatory CoS gates. Historical roster roles do not constitute live assignments.
sourceEvidence.implication: All packages must retain the Part I acceptance/founder gate for implementation; this crosswalk records authorized preparation only.

sourceEvidence.title: Existing control-plane contracts and consumer inventory
sourceEvidence.observation: Existing tenant, entity-reference, proposal and queue schemas are reuse anchors. The targeted non-test reference search finds AgentQueueEnvelopeV1 only in its definition/parser file; this does not establish a universal runtime consumer.
sourceEvidence.implication: Trace each API, service and worker consumer when introducing OM contracts; a contract file or prior inventory is not integration acceptance.

sourceEvidence.title: Trusted action lifecycle and receipts
sourceEvidence.observation: Approval/execution read expected versions before state-based transition predicates. Outbound receipts remain executing/queued with the explicit provider-disabled note; legacy execution_succeeded terminology exists.
sourceEvidence.implication: OM-02 must prove atomic version/expiry behavior. OM-03 must connect durable dispatch and provider reconciliation. A30 forbids treating this queued receipt as delivery, booking, cash or mission success. These are source-review risks, not reproduced production failures.

sourceEvidence.title: Merged consent foundation with bounded enablement
sourceEvidence.observation: The merged foundation has versioned consent checks and revocation paths. The generic decision writer is gated by CONSENT_RECEIPT_BOUNDARY_ACTIVE; challenge delivery is gated by customerEmailVerificationDeliveryEnabled. Source defaults do not prove deployed configuration.
sourceEvidence.implication: Reuse #430 and earlier #301 work. Full capture/provider-boundary and STOP race evidence remain prerequisites for affected outbound workflows; do not describe all consent work as absent.

sourceEvidence.title: Integration outbox and audit
sourceEvidence.observation: Existing createOrGetIntegrationOutboxOperation opens its own tenant transaction and stores operation/audit identity.
sourceEvidence.implication: Reuse the ledger, but design a shared transaction boundary for action authorization and dispatch intent. Existing separate transactions do not by themselves prove atomic action/outbox claims.

sourceEvidence.title: Current queue and worker consumers
sourceEvidence.observation: BullMQ queues, queue policy registry and worker bootstrap are current source anchors.
sourceEvidence.implication: OM workers must use trusted tenant envelopes, persisted waits, leases and reconciliation within this stack; do not infer source flags equal active deployment.

sourceEvidence.title: Revenue outcomes and proposal consumers
sourceEvidence.observation: jobRevenue uses positive amountPaid, then invoiceTotal, then estimateTotal; the existing contribution calculation is not a complete labor/overhead cost model. Proposal builders provide existing estimate, payment and retention integration points.
sourceEvidence.implication: OM-04 must isolate versioned earned/invoiced/cash projections and completeness. OM-10/12 must reuse proposal services without treating proposals as executed outcomes.

sourceEvidence.title: Owned intake and authoritative booking
sourceEvidence.observation: Existing intake and booking services are source/commitment anchors.
sourceEvidence.implication: OM-05/09/10 must preserve source identity and share manual, self-service and OM feasibility/reservation constraints. No second intake database or booking scheduler.

sourceEvidence.title: Inventory and dispatch domain services
sourceEvidence.observation: Existing inventory records and dispatch ranking supply domain data and command boundaries.
sourceEvidence.implication: OM-08/10 extend verification, material and qualification rules; unverified stock is not zero and rankings cannot waive hard feasibility constraints.

sourceEvidence.title: Command Center consumers and design governance
sourceEvidence.observation: Current Command Center API/web consumers and canonical Figma requirements already exist.
sourceEvidence.implication: OM-06 extends these consumers after contract reconciliation; exact frame/state/breakpoint evidence and independent acceptance are still required. The pending UI stack is not part of this pinned baseline.

sourceEvidence.title: Current provider extension points
sourceEvidence.observation: The inspected GBP and call-tracking registries have disabled/default extension behavior. They are not proof of a completed Google Search campaign executor.
sourceEvidence.implication: OM-09 requires named connector/account/budget/receipt evidence and an explicit scope extension beyond FS-266's ad-buying non-goal.

sourceEvidence.title: Model observability boundary
sourceEvidence.observation: Existing AI observability can be reused; it does not establish OM task schemas, concurrent budget reservations or evaluated escalation policy.
sourceEvidence.implication: OM-07 adds bounded capability contracts, usage/evaluation integration and explicit unavailable states.

sourceEvidence.title: Existing finance and agreement domains
sourceEvidence.observation: Existing invoice and agreement services retain authoritative financial/contract state.
sourceEvidence.implication: OM-04/12 project source facts and invoke existing authorized paths. New enrollment needs accepted terms, obligations and supported billing; payment movement is separately gated.

sourceEvidence.title: Authoritative schema
sourceEvidence.observation: This is the authoritative schema location; existing tenant/domain tables and outbox/consent structures must be considered before new storage.
sourceEvidence.implication: Serialize schema ownership, migration index selection and explicit RLS with implementation. Proposed om_* names in the source spec are design targets, not existing tables or reserved migrations.

sourceEvidence.title: Historical audit and current preparation inventory
sourceEvidence.observation: Existing audits and inventory documents are reusable evidence indexes, each with its original scope/date/status.
sourceEvidence.implication: Do not promote historical conclusions to current runtime PASS. Target changed consumers at the eventual implementation head and retain required review gates.

fileConsumerCoordination.rule: Agree versions, trusted tenant derivation and mutation idempotency/version semantics first. Update API, typed clients, workers and UI consumers together; do not assume the current queue schema is universally wired.

fileConsumerCoordination.area: Central schema, RLS and migration order
fileConsumerCoordination.rule: One explicit schema coordinator at implementation time; sequence migrations against the current journal/open PRs, include RLS and tenant references, and do not reserve a migration index in preparation.

fileConsumerCoordination.area: Trusted actions, consent, dispatch and receipts
fileConsumerCoordination.rule: Resolve the action/outbox transaction seam and shared consent/grant checks before adapters. Coordinate any STOP/provider-boundary changes with existing Part I owners rather than layering a duplicate sender.

Version the OM projection independently from legacy totals, preserve invoice/payment/agreement source truth and non-additive contributor links, and coordinate every existing reporting consumer affected by a semantic change.
Review hard feasibility and atomic reservation semantics across OM, manual dispatch, self-service and inventory consumers; OM references domain-owned reservations.
Agree canonical finding keys, coverage/freshness and condition-specific evidence; scan code must not mutate stock or claim physical verification.

fileConsumerCoordination.area: Command Center and pending UI stack
fileConsumerCoordination.rule: Reconcile against accepted contracts and the #432 → #435 → #437 → #438 integration sequence. Rebase and repeat only affected consumer/design checks at the eventual reviewed head.
Keep task dispatch, token/cost reservations, one bounded repair and output validation consistent; no model may publish or write authoritative domain state.

Select reviewed adapter locations after scope ownership. Revalidate live provider capabilities and costs at implementation; keep Render experiments independent, disabled and outside the core critical path.

reconciliationRules: Do not create replacement FS-262–269 tickets, duplicate FS-257/258, reopen historical Done features or infer runtime ownership from an anchor.
Preserve the original valid scope and acceptance references; record the delta explicitly before implementation.
Keep FS-263 contract-only unless its scope is explicitly amended. Record runtime ownership separately.
Resolve Google Search connector scope beyond FS-266's explicit ad-buying exclusion under OM-D12; first check existing ownership before any new child ticket.
Keep all implementation owners unassigned and all observed Backlog statuses unchanged.
Only applicable optional acceptance gates may block an adopted optional capability; disabled/unadvertised Render evaluation does not block core OM.
Recheck source paths, dependencies, ticket/PR heads and missing decisions at implementation time. A preparation fixture or historical source audit cannot satisfy runtime acceptance.
